A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 24-page MOSAIC paper, including appendices A–J. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching scientific content; the first-page arXiv version/date stamp differs.

before.justification: v1 reports original MOSAIC experiments on agentic safety, benign tool use and privacy, including benchmark results in Tables 1–4 and ablations in Tables 5 and 7.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original benchmark experiments, training analyses and ablation results, including those in the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same plan–check–act/refuse procedure, optional safety reasoning, pairwise preference rewards and GRPO training.

E1.justification: Both retain Agent-SafetyBench training and evaluation on AgentHarm, Agent Security Bench, BFCLv3 and PrivacyLens, with identical task and scenario coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains GPT-4o, GPT-5 and the same open-weight base-model comparisons. Tables 5 and 7 retain the same think-only and pointwise-reward comparators.

E3.justification: Section 3 and Appendices B, C and I retain identical evaluation protocols, metrics, model configurations and training settings, including all entries in Table 8.

E4.justification: The safety-check and reward ablations, token-efficiency analyses, judge positional-bias analysis and appendix rollout case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is identical, including Figure 3's 95% confidence bands for fitted response-length trends. Run, seed and significance-test reporting does not change.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 retains Qwen2.5 harm scores of 0.18 for the base model and 0.09 for MOSAIC; appendix ablation values also remain identical.

T1.justification: The action and trajectory definitions, pairwise preference aggregation and composite reward equations in Section 2 and Algorithm 1 are identical. No formal assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about explicit safety decisions, preference-based training, generalization and token efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including the model-specific safety–utility trade-offs in Section 4.2 and the judge positional-bias discussion in Appendix D.

D1.justification: The hardware and verl implementation description, appendix prompts, judge configurations and Table 8 hyperparameters are identical. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 5, the bibliography and the positioning relative to external safeguards and prior preference-learning work are unchanged.

P1.justification: Only the first-page marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 3 March 2026 to v2 dated 3 June 2026. Paper prose, terminology, headings and section order are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5, Tables 1–8, captions and page layout are unchanged. Rendered differences are confined to the marginal version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: The complete main text and appendices retain identical methods, evidence, interpretations and reproducibility information. Updating the arXiv stamp and its corresponding version link does not meaningfully affect paper quality.
